subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
subtype: Approach: reviewing the call and adjusting communication cadence [Revision]
passage: Review note after the client call, written by Deepika, delivery manager. I sat in on Chaitanya's call with the client on Tuesday. The client was not angry about the delay itself. They said twice that they had found out late and wanted to hear from us more often. Afterwards Chaitanya and I sat with the team and went through the notes. A weekly email was clearly not enough. We changed it: a short note every Monday and Thursday, three lines each: done, next, worries. Chaitanya wrote the first one that afternoon. A week later the client replied, "This is what I needed," and stopped phoning the account manager directly. I will keep watching for three weeks to check it is not turning into a chore.

qa.q: On which days do the short notes go out?
qa.a: The short notes go out every Monday and Thursday.

qa.q: What was the client feeling about the way they were kept informed?
qa.a: The client felt left in the dark and worried, having found out late and wanting to hear more often.

qa.q: What else could the team do to keep the notes useful, and why?
qa.a: The team could ask the client after a month whether three lines are enough, because the right rhythm may change as the project moves.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya have felt after the client's reply?
qa.a: Chaitanya probably felt relieved and encouraged, since a small change in habit had steadied the relationship.

grounding: Illustrates reviewing a client call, finding the client wanted more frequent updates and switching to short Monday and Thursday notes.

subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
subtype: Approach: reviewing the call and adjusting communication cadence [Revision]
passage:
Thursday, late

Call with Jaya's logistics team today about the delayed warehouse software. Went okay on the surface. But near the end Jaya said, "I just don't want to be surprised again," and I wrote it down without really thinking.
After the call, Farooq and I replayed it. He pointed out that Jaya asked "when will we hear next?" three separate times. Three! We've been sending one long email every Friday, and by Friday she's already been chased by her own boss for days.
So we're changing it. Short notes every Monday and Thursday, five lines max: what moved, what's stuck, what's next. Farooq will draft, I'll send.
Felt a bit silly that we missed something so obvious. But Jaya replied to the first test note tonight with just "This helps. Thank you."
Small thing. Big relief.
— Sabina

qa.q: How many times did Jaya ask when they would hear next?
qa.a: Jaya asked "when will we hear next?" three separate times.

qa.q: How did Sabina feel after the team missed Jaya's repeated question?
qa.a: Sabina felt a bit silly for missing something so obvious, and then relieved when Jaya replied that the new note helped.

qa.q: What other approach could have caught Jaya's need even earlier?
qa.a: The team could have asked at the start of the project how often and in what form the client wanted updates, instead of choosing a weekly email for her.

qa.q: How does the change look from Jaya's side?
qa.a: Jaya no longer waits a whole week while her boss chases her; short notes twice a week let her answer questions and feel less surprised.

grounding: It shows a team reviewing a client call, noticing the client wanted more frequent updates, and switching to short twice-weekly notes so the relationship steadies.

Zainab: ok so the call with the bank ended. how did I sound?
Yusuf: calm. but did you notice what their project head kept saying?
Zainab: "we haven't heard anything since last Friday" 😬
Yusuf: exactly. twice. they're not upset about the delay, they're upset about the silence
Zainab: we send the weekly email though
Yusuf: a week is long when your go-live has slipped
Zainab: fair. what if we switch to short notes on Monday and Thursday? three bullets, done/stuck/next
Yusuf: I'll draft Monday's. you do Thursday's
Zainab: deal. telling them now so it's official
Zainab: two weeks later update: their head just replied "much better rhythm now, thanks" 🙂
Yusuf: see, no new plan, just more often 😊

qa.q: What did the bank's project head keep saying on the call?
qa.a: The project head kept saying, "we haven't heard anything since last Friday."

qa.q: How can you tell Zainab was anxious straight after the call?
qa.a: Zainab immediately asks Yusuf how the call sounded and adds a grimacing emoji when recalling the client's complaint, which suggests Zainab was worried it had gone badly.

qa.q: What could Zainab and Yusuf try if the twice-weekly notes had not helped?
qa.a: They could ask the bank's project head directly what kind of update would help most, such as a short call, rather than guessing the format.

qa.q: What is the change like for the bank's project head?
qa.a: The project head no longer waits a week in silence, so the delay feels managed and the relationship becomes calmer.

grounding: It shows a team reviewing a client call, noticing the client wanted more frequent contact, and moving from weekly emails to short Monday and Thursday notes.
